title: Mitchigamea language - Wikipedia
text: Mitchigamea or Michigamea is an extinct language formerly spoken by the Mitchigamea people in Arkansas. In 1673, Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet asked a Mitchigamea man, who only spoke Illinois poorly, to be a translator between the Illinois-speaking French, and the Dhegihan-speaking Quapaw. [1]

title: Mitchigamea - Wikipedia
text: The Michigamea were a Native American tribe in the Illinois Confederation. The Mitchigamea may have spoken an Algonquian [1] or a Siouan-Catawban language, and historical accounts describe them as not being fluent in the Illinois language.
